task.description: Design the ISS-0437 fix: eviction of a deactivated tenant's entry from Letflow.Admission's state, closing a real fairness bug (permanent dilution of other tenants' fair-share cap).

result.note: Design doc written to lib/letflow/design/iss0437-admission-tenant-eviction.md (343 lines). New Letflow.Admission.forget_tenant/2 client API, defaulting server to __MODULE__, handled by a new handle_call({:forget_tenant, schema}, ...) clause that unconditionally deletes the schema key from state.tenants, idempotent on an absent key. In-use handling: eviction is unconditional regardless of in_use count -- refusing eviction was rejected (no retry trigger exists), force-zeroing-but-keeping was rejected (reintroduces the dilution bug one level down). The real consequence (a race where an in-flight Ref later calls release/2 against a now-missing key) is handled by hardening release_tenant/2 to treat a missing schema key as a no-op rather than raising KeyError via its current Map.update!/3. Wiring: NOT inside Letflow.Identity.deactivate_tenant/1 -- design found and followed an existing precedent (Identity.create_tenant/1 explicitly does not call TenantProvisioning itself, that orchestration happens at the router layer) -- forget_tenant/1 is called from Letflow.Routers.Tenants's deactivate handler after Identity.deactivate_tenant/1 succeeds, keeping Identity free of any Admission dependency. Reactivation needs zero additional code -- ensure_tenant_tracked/2's existing lazy-creation-on-first-attempt behavior already handles it, stated explicitly. REQ-216 doc corrections specified verbatim for two locations (admission.ex moduledoc, req216 design doc SS3/SS9 OQ-2) stating eviction now happens but only on deactivation, not a general time-window mechanism. Three tests specified: a genuine fairness test (per_tenant_cap/1's gating behavior actually changes, not just key removal), a race test (evicting an in-use tenant doesn't crash a subsequent release), a reactivation regression guard. One open question flagged (SS7): how to assert the new router-level call against the real application-supervised Admission process given no server-parameter seam exists at the router layer today -- left for ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER, not silently resolved. Scope confirmed: no change to try_acquire/2's algorithm or per_tenant_cap/1's formula, no route/controller signature changes beyond the one addition inside the existing deactivate handler, no new config. Self-checked: grepped for defmodule/def/schema-do/Enum./fn / patterns, zero real matches -- only inline @spec/@type signatures and prose.
